bib.title: MathQA: Towards Interpretable Math Word Problem Solving with Operation-Based Formalisms

question: How can math word problems be annotated with precise, interpretable operation programs at scale, and can a neural sequence-to-program model trained on them solve the problems?
hypothesis: Training on operation-program supervision in a domain-aware representation language improves accuracy and interpretability over models trained on noisy AQuA rationales.
contributions: We introduce a large-scale dataset of math word problems that are densely annotated with operation programs
We introduce a new representation language to model operation programs corresponding to each math problem that aim to improve both the performance and the interpretability of the learned models.
We introduce a neural architecture leveraging a sequence-to-program model with automatic problem categorization, achieving competitive results on our dataset as well as the AQuA dataset

method.summary: MathQA re-annotates a solvable subset of AQuA-RAT with operation programs in a 58-operation, category-aware representation language, using crowd workers on Figure Eight with validation. An attention LSTM encoder-decoder (OpenNMT) maps problem text to an operation program; programs are executed and matched to the multiple-choice options. A variant switches decoder LSTM parameters by a hard n-gram-derived domain category.
method.task: math word problem solving via operation-program generation (multiple choice)

datasets.name: MathQA
datasets.source: annotated subset of AQuA-RAT (Ling et al., 2017); crowd annotation on Figure Eight; dataset at math-qa.github.io/math-QA/
datasets.preprocessing: Categorised into Geometry, Physics, Probability, Gain-Loss, General, Other by n-gram frequency; annotation expansion to similar AQuA problems via Levenshtein distance threshold of 4 words with numbers replaced by generic numbers

datasets.name: AQuA-RAT
datasets.split: original AQuA split; of the train set 65,991 solvable, 17,294 duplicates
datasets.preprocessing: Models for AQuA are trained on MathQA data; problems outside any MathQA category get a random option

models.name: Seq2prog
models.architecture: attention-based bidirectional RNN encoder, LSTM decoder, OpenNMT
models.vocab: 58 operations plus argument slots (constants, problem numbers by position, intermediate results by order)

models.name: Seq2prog + cat
models.architecture: Seq2prog with a separate decoder LSTM parameter set per domain category (hard switch)

models.name: AQuA Model
models.architecture: state-of-the-art model on AQuA (Ling et al., 2017), described as much more complex

training.objective: negative log-likelihood of the gold operation program given the problem text

inference.decoding: beam search, beam size 200 for AQuA and 100 for MathQA; each beam program executed; options within a threshold of the executed value are selected, then the program with the fewest selected options and minimum distance to an option is chosen

parameters.random_fallback: random option for AQuA problems outside any MathQA category

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of test problems where the option matched by the executed predicted program is correct

eval.protocol: single reported run per model; no seeds or significance test stated

limits: Evaluation is a single run per model; no seeds, variance or significance tests; batch size, epochs and hardware are not stated.
Authors concede the categorization gain is small because categories are only hard decoding constraints and the n-gram categorization is noisy.
Representation omits high-order polynomials, sequence problems, factorization and entirely nonnumeric solutions; results remain well below human performance (no human number printed).
Multiple-choice matching by executed value means accuracy can include lucky option matches; the 20.0 random baseline assumes 5 options.
Dataset size printed as 37,200 in text and 37,259 in Table 1; AQuA-derived problems carry residual noise and near-duplicates.
Models are 2019 LSTM seq2seq; LLM-era evaluation of MathQA differs from this setup.

terms.definition: a sequence with n operations o1(a1)o2(a2)...on(an), each operation taking a list of arguments that may be prior step outputs
